CCONJ.title: written attached
CCONJ.why: وَ and فَ are written together with the next word.

CCONJ.title: what follows
CCONJ.why: لٰكِنَّ takes a noun in the accusative or a pronoun suffix; the others join words or whole clauses.

INTJ.title: transliteration
INTJ.why: Shows the vowels of the formula.

INTJ.title: said to
INTJ.why: Many formulas change with the person addressed: a man, a woman, a group (كَيْفَ حَالُكَ / حَالُكِ / حَالُكُمْ).

INTJ.title: fixed answer
INTJ.why: The answer this formula gets (صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ → صَبَاحُ النُّورِ); “none” when there is no fixed answer.

NOUN.title: gender
NOUN.why: Drives the agreement of adjectives, verbs and pronouns and the polarity of the numbers 3–10.

NOUN.title: transliteration
NOUN.why: Shows the vowels and the sounds until the script is read fluently: the pausal form, without case or tanwīn ending (kitāb, muḥāmī, maqhā).

NOUN.title: root (radicals)
NOUN.why: Links the word to its family and to the dictionary; “none” for loanwords and for phrases (their parts have their own roots).

NOUN.title: pattern (wazn)
NOUN.why: The measure in ف ع ل letters (mafʿal = place, mifʿāl = tool, fāʿil = doer …) lets the learner guess new words; “none” for loanwords, phrases and words that fit no measure.

NOUN.title: sun letter (al- assimilates)
NOUN.why: With a sun letter the l of the article is not pronounced and the letter is doubled: الشَّمْسُ aš-šams; with a moon letter: الْقَمَرُ al-qamar.

NOUN.title: human (agreement class)
NOUN.why: Plurals of people agree in the plural; all other plurals agree as feminine singular (الْكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ).

NOUN.title: plurals
NOUN.why: The plural is learned with the noun: its kind (broken, sound masculine -ūna, sound feminine -āt), its pattern and declension, and the meanings it belongs to (بُيُوت houses / أَبْيَات verses). “none” for mass nouns, names and words used only in the singular.

NOUN.title: dual
NOUN.why: Mostly regular (-āni), but ة becomes ت (سَنَتَانِ) and some duals are irregular (أَبَوَانِ); “none” for mass nouns, names and plural-only words.

NOUN.title: declension (of the singular; of the head noun in a phrase)
NOUN.why: Triptotes take tanwīn and -i in the genitive; diptotes (names, أَفْعَل, -ān, many broken plurals) take no tanwīn and -a; defective nouns end in -in (مُحَامٍ); invariable nouns never change (مَقْهًى، كُوسَا).

NOUN.title: unit noun
NOUN.why: One piece of a collective (تُفَّاحَة from تُفَّاح); needed for counting.

NOUN.title: forms of one meaning only
NOUN.why: A form (a fixed phrase, another maṣdar, an adverbial accusative …) that belongs to one meaning of the word; “none” when every meaning has the same forms. Per-meaning plurals are in plurals.

PRON.title: person, number, gender
PRON.why: Gender in the 2nd and 3rd person (أَنْتَ / أَنْتِ، هُمْ / هُنَّ).

PRON.title: attached form
PRON.why: The pronoun as an ending on nouns, verbs and prepositions (كِتَابُكَ، يَرَاهُ، لَهَا).

VERB.title: transliteration
VERB.why: Shows the vowels of the 3rd person singular past (the citation form).

VERB.title: root (radicals)
VERB.why: The verb is the centre of its word family.

VERB.title: root class
VERB.why: Weak radicals (و ي), a doubled radical or hamza change the conjugation: hollow قَالَ، defective مَشَى، assimilated وَصَلَ، doubled أَحَبَّ، hamzated أَكَلَ.

VERB.title: verb form
VERB.why: Form I … X gives the present, participle and maṣdar patterns and a typical meaning.

VERB.title: present (imperfect) 3rd person singular
VERB.why: The second principal part: the stem vowel of form I (يَكْتُبُ / يَشْرَبُ / يَجْلِسُ) cannot be predicted. “none” for a verb that has no present.

VERB.title: verbal noun (maṣdar)
VERB.why: Arabic’s “infinitive” (to eat = أَكْل); unpredictable for form I. “none” for a verb that has none.

VERB.title: active / passive participle
VERB.why: Very frequent as nouns and adjectives (كَاتِب writer, مَكْتُوب written); the passive participle only for verbs with an object.

VERB.title: object and preposition
VERB.why: What the verb takes: a direct object (accusative) or a preposition (ذَهَبَ إِلَى، خَرَجَ مِنْ، اِنْتَظَرَ + acc.), per meaning. “none” for a verb used without an object.

VERB.title: forms of one meaning only
VERB.why: A form (a fixed phrase, another maṣdar, an adverbial accusative …) that belongs to one meaning of the word; “none” when every meaning has the same forms. Per-meaning plurals are in plurals.
